According to the Second Law of Thermodynamics, the total entropy of the universe always increases and can never decrease [d8]. Assuming the universe is an isolated system, its total entropy is continually increasing [d8], and entropy is generated everywhere and always at any scale without exception — it cannot be destroyed by any means [d1]. For every change that occurs, the entropy of the universe as a whole must increase, even if local entropy (such as in a freezing system) decreases, because the entropy released to the surroundings more than compensates [d4]. Even during the inflationary epoch of the early universe, when entropy density dropped dramatically as the universe expanded, the overall entropy of the universe never decreased — it was only the entropy density that went down as volume increased exponentially [d7]. This relentless increase in entropy is predicted to culminate in a "heat death" of the universe, where everything reaches the same temperature and no more work can be done [d2]. All processes convert low-entropy, useful energy into high-entropy, useless energy, constrained by the entropy law [d6].
